scoring_justification: All scored artifacts are derived quantities from MD simulations; compare to paper-reported thresholds/trends with tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Thresholds and reference trends for HM ratio, aCNA fractions, persistence diagram rings, pressure-dependent HM ratio, and enthalpy relations derived from paper's main text.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig.2(a) H/M reaches ~4 at ~120 ps; Fig.2(b) fcc Ca reaches ~86% after quenching (thermal underestimation); Fig.3 persistence diagram ring (b,d)≈(1.0,2.1); Fig.4(a) final H/M vs pressure; Fig.4(b) ΔH_fus+hyd < ΔH_fus above 30 GPa.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Inline thresholds and trend rules extracted from paper; gold values are aligned to paper claims and tolerances designed to be reachable by a faithful re-run.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Numbers are based on the paper's reported quantitative observations; thresholds are chosen to be reachable by any faithful reproduction while excluding random guesses.

outputs.description: Time evolution of the hydrogen-to-metal ratio during the CaH₂(100)/H₂ MLP-MD simulation at 1500 K and 40 GPa.
Adaptive common neighbor analysis of the Ca sublattice during the same simulation; the quenched fcc fraction is derived from this time series or its tail.
Time-averaged persistence diagram ring features for the hydrogenating condition and reference bulk CaH₄.
Final H/M ratio after 1 ns for each pressure-scan condition.
Pressure-dependent fusion enthalpy of CaH₄ and formation enthalpy of liquid CaH₄ from CaH₂ + H₂.

output_contract.notes: All scored outputs are compared against hidden reference thresholds or structural relations derived from the paper. Agent must execute the full pipeline (DFT, MLP training, MD) to produce correct artifacts.

steps.description: H/M ratio must reach >= 3.8 within 100–200 ps
Final fcc Ca fraction >= 0.6 averaged over last 20 ps
Ring feature (b,d) ≈ (1.0,2.1) present in both persistence_pairs and reference_bulk_CaH4
Hydrogenation only for (100) at 1500K ≥30 GPa (HM>3.5); others <2.5
